text: I'll start with the paged workload.

arguments.root_cause_statement: Service payments/payments-gateway selects pods with label app=payments-gateway, but the only backing workload, Deployment payments/payments-gateway-api, stamps its pods with app=payments-gateway-api. No pod matches the selector, so Endpoints payments/payments-gateway carries no addresses and its ClusterIP 10.96.191.39 refuses connections. Deployment storefront/checkout-api resolves http://payments-gateway:8080/health through the ExternalName Service storefront/payments-gateway to that same ClusterIP, logs "payment gateway UNREACHABLE ... - holding checkout submissions", never touches /tmp/ready, and so both replicas fail their exec readiness probe and report 0/2 Ready while checkout submissions are held.
arguments.mechanism: Service payments/payments-gateway has .spec.selector set to app=payments-gateway while the pods created by Deployment payments/payments-gateway-api carry the label app=payments-gateway-api, so the selector matches nothing and Endpoints payments/payments-gateway is created with no addresses. With no backend behind ClusterIP 10.96.191.39, TCP to port 8080 gets "wget: can't connect to remote host (10.96.191.39): Connection refused", which is what callers of the gateway health endpoint receive.

evidence.claim: Both checkout-api pods run but never pass their readiness probe, so the Deployment reports 0/2.
The readiness probe on the checkout-api pod is failing.
checkout-api holds checkout submissions because the payment gateway ClusterIP refuses connections.
evidence.quote: wget: can't connect to remote host (10.96.191.39): Connection refused

evidence.claim: The refused address is the ClusterIP of Service payments/payments-gateway, reached via the storefront ExternalName alias.
storefront/payments-gateway is an ExternalName alias pointing at the payments namespace service.
The payments Service selector matches no pods; the running gateway pods are labelled differently.
The Deployment's pod template label is app=payments-gateway-api, not app=payments-gateway.
Endpoints payments/payments-gateway has no subsets at all.

ruled_out.alternative: The gateway backend pods are themselves down or unhealthy
ruled_out.ruling_claim: Both gateway pods are Running and Ready with no restarts, so the backend process is healthy; only the Service selector fails to reach them.
ruled_out.quote: pod/payments-gateway-api-9c78bc7b-k65l8 phase=Running labels={app=payments-gateway-api, pod-template-hash=9c78bc7b} node=incident-lab-control-plane gateway(ready=True,restarts=0)

ruled_out.alternative: The storefront ExternalName Service points at the wrong DNS name
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The ExternalName resolves to payments-gateway.payments.svc.cluster.local, which is exactly the Service that exists in the payments namespace and whose ClusterIP the pod actually reached.

ruled_out.alternative: checkout-api's own container or probe is misconfigured (bad image, crash, missing config)
ruled_out.ruling_claim: The container started cleanly with zero restarts and its ConfigMap volume mounted; it is running and merely reporting the gateway unreachable.
ruled_out.quote:
State:          Running
      Started:      Wed, 02 Sep 2026 08:40:15 +0530
    Ready:          False
    Restart Count:  0

verification.command: kubectl -n payments get endpoints payments-gateway -o yaml
kubectl -n payments get svc payments-gateway -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'
